articles.fullText:
South African President Cyril Ramaphosa addressing leaders from the 16-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) at a summit in Durban, South Africa, August 17, 2026. /South African Presidencya has called on regional leaders to work together to address migration after weeks of anti-migrant protests forced more than 176,000 people to leave the country.
Ramaphosa addressed leaders from the 16-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) at a summit in Durban on Monday, where he described migration as a major regional challenge.
"We thanked countries in our region for their understanding of the challenges that we faced and, in some respects, continue to face," Ramaphosa said as he closed the summit. "We also expressed regret at what has befallen us as a country. We expressed a wish that we should all work together to address the challenge of migration."
The flags of the nations representing the 16-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) at a summit in Durban, South Africa, August 17, 2026. /South African Presidency
The exodus followed weeks of protests by populist groups demanding that undocumented foreign nationals leave South Africa by June 30.
More than 176,000 people have left the country in recent weeks, according to an AFP tally based on figures provided by African governments. About 300 anti-migrant protesters marched to the summit venue on Monday, urging regional leaders to "fetch their people".
Police on horseback and motorbikes controlled the demonstration as a helicopter and drones monitored the gathering.
"We are here to tell you to come and fetch your people who are here in South Africa illegally," said protest leader Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, one of the figures behind the recent demonstrations.
She singled out Malawi, Mozambique and Zimbabwe, whose nationals accounted for most of those who left South Africa.
Some migrants departed voluntarily, while others were deported or assisted through government repatriation programs.
Migrant deaths spark condemnation
At least four migrants were killed during the violence, according to South African police, although some foreign governments have reported a higher death toll.
Ramaphosa said during a public lecture on Friday that his government was "deeply concerned and ashamed" that nationals of other countries had in recent months been subjected to discrimination and ill-treatment.
The South African government's handling of the unrest has drawn criticism from other African countries, including Ghana and Nigeria, which are not members of SADC.
South Africa, which assumed the rotating SADC chairmanship at Monday's summit, has called for an Africa-wide conference on migration.
Attendees at the 16-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) summit in Durban, South Africa, August 17, 2026. /South African Presidency
Ramaphosa's government says a broader continental approach is needed to address the causes of migration, improve cooperation between countries and prevent tensions between host communities and migrants from escalating into violence.
South Africa has long been a major destination for migrants from across the continent, attracted by its relatively developed economy and employment opportunities.
But the country is also grappling with unemployment of more than 30%, deep inequality and widespread poverty, conditions that have fuelled public anger and intensified political pressure over immigration.
The latest unrest has renewed debate over how South Africa and its neighbours can manage migration while protecting the rights and safety of migrants.

articles.fullText:
The UK government has announced plans to invest more in robotic equipment for English hospitals and set a target for robotic assistance to be used in 90% of keyhole surgeries carried out in England by 2035.
The government highlighted robotics as one of five "big bets" in a 10-year health plan for England, alongside other transformative technologies: data, AI, genomics and wearables.
Surgeons and nurses using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing surgery, at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
At St Bartholomew's Hospital in central London, visiting surgeons are among the first to be trained to use the new da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, made by US company Initiative. The system, which includes three robotic arms that can hold surgical equipment, is controlled using an immersive 3D headset and a video-game-like console.
Robotic surgical systems like this can be used across a range of specialties including urology, gynecology, abdominal, colorectal, and thoracic or general surgery.
Sasha Stamenkovic (C) using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system while performing lung cancer surgery as Ali Ansaripour (R), senior cardiothoracic trainee on a robotic fellowship, looks on. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
The precision of robotic-assisted surgery should mean shorter hospital stays and quicker recovery times, which will take strain off a struggling health service with year-long waitlists, workforce shortages and discharge bottlenecks.
"The ability to have lots of integrated computer-aided technology on top" of human-controlled robotics "makes this precise surgery. It makes it safe surgery," says Sasha Stamenkovic, Director of Robotic Surgery and Research at Barts Health NHS Trust.
As well as improving recovery times, the greater precision also reduces the risk of complications like air leaks, a common cause of longer hospital stays following lung surgery.
Nurses assisting in lung cancer surgery using the new Da Vinci 5 robotic-assisted surgical system, at St Bartholomew's Hospital. /Carlos Jasso/AFP
Ian Macleod was the first patient in Britain's NHS to undergo lung cancer surgery using the new da Vinci robotic system. Macleod says he "didn't realize" until he was wearing a surgical gown and anesthetised that he would hold this groundbreaking title, but the news "didn't faze" the 76-year-old retired detective.
Thirty minutes after the robotic-assisted operation, Macleod was back on his feet. "It was extraordinary," he says. "In fact, after the operation, I found out quite quickly that I only had one stitch." He had undergone non-robotic keyhole surgery for a different cancer in the past, and says the recovery time was "much longer". This time, he was driving his wife to the garden centrer for coffee less than a week later.
Stamenkovic runs fellowships at St Bartholomew's training surgeons on this new technology. He says it is the young surgeons who pick up the new robotic control system the fastest and who become the most adept.
"They've come with different skill sets," he says, "they've probably come with gaming skill sets, some of them have come with a musical background."
Laying out his long-term mission, Stamenkovic added: "All we need to do is harness their energy, their passion, their skill set, and teach them the right moves. And that will make the surgeon of the future."

此类机器人手术系统可用于多种专科，包括泌尿科、妇科、腹部、结直肠、胸外科或普外科。Sasha Stamenkovic（中）使用新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统进行肺癌手术，Ali Ansaripour（右）作为机器人专科高级心胸外科培训生在一旁观看。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

机器人辅助手术的精准性应能缩短住院时间并加快恢复速度，这将缓解一个面临年长候诊名单、劳动力短缺和出院瓶颈的艰难医疗系统的压力。“在人类控制的机器人技术之上集成大量计算机辅助技术的能力，使这种手术精准。它使手术安全，”巴特斯健康NHS信托机器人手术与研究主任Sasha Stamenkovic说。

除了改善恢复时间，更高的精准度还降低了并发症风险，如肺手术后常见的导致住院时间延长的漏气。护士在圣巴塞洛缪医院使用新型达芬奇5机器人辅助手术系统协助肺癌手术。/Carlos Jasso/AFP

Ian Macleod是英国NHS中首位使用新型达芬奇机器人系统进行肺癌手术的患者。Macleod说，直到穿上手术服并被麻醉，他才意识到自己将拥有这一开创性头衔，但这一消息“没有吓到”这位76岁的退休侦探。机器人辅助手术后30分钟，Macleod就重新站了起来。

“这太不寻常了，”他说。“事实上，手术后我很快发现我只有一针缝合。”他过去曾因另一种癌症接受过非机器人微创手术，并表示恢复时间“长得多”。这次，不到一周后他就开车带妻子去花园中心喝咖啡。Stamenkovic在圣巴塞洛缪医院开展奖学金项目，培训外科医生使用这项新技术。他说，年轻外科医生掌握新机器人控制系统最快，也最熟练。

“他们带来了不同的技能组合，”他说，“他们可能带来了游戏技能，有些人有音乐背景。”

Stamenkovic阐述了他的长期使命：“我们只需要利用他们的能量、热情和技能，教他们正确的动作。这将造就未来的外科医生。”

articles.title: Europe faces record heat, drought and water-related pressures
articles.titleCn: 欧洲面临创纪录高温、干旱和水资源压力
articles.summary: Europe faces record heat, drought and water-related pressures
articles.summaryCn: 欧洲正经历极端高温和干旱，导致河流水位下降、野火频发，并对农业、能源和公共健康造成严重影响。

paragraphs.en: Europe is experiencing a summer of extreme heat and drought, with record temperatures, wildfire risks and falling river levels affecting several countries. A {{0}} landscape in the wake of a wildfire that swept through the Gironde region in Lege-Cap-Ferret, southwestern France, August 4, 2026. France recorded its hottest July since nationwide records began in 1900, with a monthly average temperature of 24.9 degrees Celsius, according to Meteo-France. Rainfall across the country was nearly 70% below the seasonal average, making July 2026 the third-driest July on record. Persistent heat, drought and windy conditions kept wildfire risks high or very high, while a wildfire in the southwestern department of Gironde burned about 42,000 hectares and forced the {{1}} of more than 220,000 people. Boats lie in the dried out riverbed of a branch of the river Danube in Hainburg, Austria, August 3, 2026.

paragraphs.en: In Austria, a national temperature record of 41 degrees Celsius was set on Tuesday as the heat wave continued. The record was measured in the Stammersdorf region of Vienna, according to Austria's state broadcaster ORF. A forest fire is also {{10}} in Burgenland, while the Lobau wetlands in Vienna face the highest fire danger level. Meanwhile, water levels on the Danube River have fallen to historically low levels, {{11}} to the major low-water years of 2003 and 2018. The dried-up Danube riverbed with the Paks power plant at the background, near Dunaszentbenedek, close to Paks town, Hungary, July 31, 2026. Neighboring Hungary has {{12}} its highest-level heat alert until midnight on Friday as {{13}} show the heat wave will continue.
paragraphs.cn: 在奥地利，随着热浪持续，周二创下了41摄氏度的全国温度记录。据奥地利国家广播公司ORF称，该记录是在维也纳的施塔默斯多夫地区测得的。布尔根兰州也正在发生森林火灾，而维也纳的洛鲍湿地面临最高火灾危险等级。与此同时，多瑙河水位已降至历史低位，与2003年和2018年的主要低水位年份相当。2026年7月31日，匈牙利敦森本德克附近，干涸的多瑙河河床，背景是帕克斯核电站。邻国匈牙利已将最高级别高温警报延长至周五午夜，因为预报显示热浪将持续。

paragraphs.en: Authorities warned that {{2}} high temperatures could affect everyone and urged people to take {{3}}. The heat wave has {{4}} drought conditions, lowered water levels in major rivers and increased wildfire risks, with firefighters recently responding to around 100 outdoor fires per day. A firefighting helicopter flies toward a wildfire on a mountain near L'Aquila, central Italy, August 3, 2026. Italy is also facing its fourth major heat wave of the summer, with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas. The Health Ministry placed 25 of the country's 27 {{14}} cities under the highest heat alert, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna, Venice, Naples and Palermo. Hot and dry conditions have increased wildfire risks and put pressure on agriculture, with farmers reporting reduced crop {{15}} and higher {{5}} demand.
paragraphs.cn: 当局警告说，持续高温可能影响所有人，并敦促人们采取预防措施。热浪加剧了干旱条件，降低了主要河流的水位，增加了野火风险，消防员最近每天应对约100起户外火灾。2026年8月3日，一架消防直升机飞向意大利中部拉奎拉附近山上的野火。意大利也面临夏季第四次大热浪，部分地区气温超过40摄氏度。卫生部将全国27个受监测城市中的25个置于最高高温警报之下，包括罗马、米兰、佛罗伦萨、博洛尼亚、威尼斯、那不勒斯和巴勒莫。炎热干燥的条件增加了野火风险，并对农业造成压力，农民报告作物减产和灌溉需求增加。

paragraphs.en: A general view of the Paks nuclear power plant, Hungary, July 31, 2026. Low river levels and rising water temperatures have also affected nuclear power operations in parts of Europe. Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which supplies nearly half of the country's electricity, remained {{16}} but its operation depended on river conditions and cooling system performance. Romania's Cernavoda nuclear power plant shut down both reactors after low Danube water levels affected operations. In France and Switzerland, some nuclear facilities also faced operational {{6}} as high river temperatures affected cooling {{7}}. The combination of extreme heat, drought and {{8}} water {{9}} is putting pressure on public health, agriculture, wildfire prevention and energy systems in affected areas.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年7月31日，匈牙利帕克斯核电站全景。低河流水位和上升的水温也影响了欧洲部分地区的核电运营。匈牙利帕克斯核电站供应全国近一半的电力，虽然仍在运营，但其运营取决于河流条件和冷却系统性能。罗马尼亚切尔纳沃德核电站在多瑙河低水位影响运营后，关闭了两个反应堆。在法国和瑞士，一些核设施也面临运营中断，因为高河流温度影响了冷却能力。极端高温、干旱和水资源减少的组合，正在对受影响地区的公共健康、农业、野火预防和能源系统造成压力。

articles.fullText:
Europe is experiencing a summer of extreme heat and drought, with record temperatures, wildfire risks and falling river levels affecting several countries.
A scorched landscape in the wake of a wildfire that swept through the Gironde region in Lege-Cap-Ferret, southwestern France, August 4, 2026. 
France recorded its hottest July since nationwide records began in 1900, with a monthly average temperature of 24.9 degrees Celsius, according to Meteo-France.
Rainfall across the country was nearly 70% below the seasonal average, making July 2026 the third-driest July on record.
Persistent heat, drought and windy conditions kept wildfire risks high or very high, while a wildfire in the southwestern department of Gironde burned about 42,000 hectares and forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people.
Boats lie in the dried out riverbed of a branch of the river Danube in Hainburg, Austria, August 3, 2026. 
In Austria, a national temperature record of 41 degrees Celsius was set on Tuesday as the heat wave continued. The record was measured in the Stammersdorf region of Vienna, according to Austria's state broadcaster ORF.
A forest fire is also raging in Burgenland, while the Lobau wetlands in Vienna face the highest fire danger level. Meanwhile, water levels on the Danube River have fallen to historically low levels, comparable to the major low-water years of 2003 and 2018.
The dried-up Danube riverbed with the Paks power plant at the background, near Dunaszentbenedek, close to Paks town, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Neighboring Hungary has extended its highest-level heat alert until midnight on Friday as forecasts show the heat wave will continue. Authorities warned that persistent high temperatures could affect everyone and urged people to take precautions.
The heat wave has intensified drought conditions, lowered water levels in major rivers and increased wildfire risks, with firefighters recently responding to around 100 outdoor fires per day.
A firefighting helicopter flies toward a wildfire on a mountain near L'Aquila, central Italy, August 3, 2026. 
Italy is also facing its fourth major heat wave of the summer, with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius in some areas.
The Health Ministry placed 25 of the country's 27 monitored cities under the highest heat alert, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Bologna, Venice, Naples and Palermo.
Hot and dry conditions have increased wildfire risks and put pressure on agriculture, with farmers reporting reduced crop yields and higher irrigation demand.
A general view of the Paks nuclear power plant, Hungary, July 31, 2026. 
Low river levels and rising water temperatures have also affected nuclear power operations in parts of Europe.
Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which supplies nearly half of the country's electricity, remained operational but its operation depended on river conditions and cooling system performance.
Romania's Cernavoda nuclear power plant shut down both reactors after low Danube water levels affected operations. In France and Switzerland, some nuclear facilities also faced operational disruptions as high river temperatures affected cooling capacity.
The combination of extreme heat, drought and declining water availability is putting pressure on public health, agriculture, wildfire prevention and energy systems in affected areas.

articles.title: Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis named Alphabet chief scientist
articles.titleCn: 诺贝尔奖得主德米斯·哈萨比斯被任命为Alphabet首席科学家
articles.summary: Google's head of AI, Demis Hassabis, will step down from his current role to become Alphabet's chief scientist amid a reshuffling at DeepMind that will also include a key engineer's departure.
articles.summaryCn: 谷歌AI负责人德米斯·哈萨比斯转任Alphabet首席科学家，同时DeepMind进行高层重组，关键工程师离职。

paragraphs.en: Google's head of AI, Demis Hassabis, will step down from his current role to become Alphabet's chief scientist amid a {{0}} at DeepMind that will also include a key engineer's departure. Hassabis will take on two new titles, Alphabet announced on Wednesday: chair of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet. The change "will allow me to focus on long-term strategy, and {{1}} scientific breakthroughs, including leaning into my work at Isomorphic to help cure disease," Hassabis wrote in a social media post. Isomorphic Labs is an AI-powered drug discovery lab that {{2}} out from DeepMind in 2021. In 2024, Hassabis won a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
paragraphs.cn: 谷歌AI负责人德米斯·哈萨比斯将卸任当前职务，成为Alphabet的首席科学家，与此同时DeepMind进行重组，包括一位关键工程师的离职。Alphabet于周三宣布，哈萨比斯将担任两个新职务：DeepMind主席和Alphabet首席科学家。哈萨比斯在社交媒体帖子中写道，这一变动“将使我能够专注于长期战略，并加速科学突破，包括深入我在Isomorphic的工作以帮助治愈疾病。”Isomorphic Labs是一个AI驱动的药物发现实验室，于2021年从DeepMind分拆出来。2024年，哈萨比斯获得了诺贝尔化学奖。

paragraphs.en: As part of the shake up, DeepMind's chief technology officer and chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu will become the division's senior vice president and {{3}} its operations, including the development of Google's {{4}} frontier models and products which are known as Gemini. Longtime Google engineer Jeff Dean is also leaving the company after nearly three decades to "try something new, and we're excited to support him in that," Google CEO Sundar Pichai said in a blog post announcing the news. Hassabis {{5}} DeepMind in 2010, and four years later, Google bought the research lab for $650 million, according to reports at the time. His co-founder, Mustafa Suleyman, is currently the chief of Microsoft's AI segment. Google is {{6}} for customers alongside other major AI developers including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, as well as DeepSeek and Moonshot in China.
paragraphs.cn: 作为重组的一部分，DeepMind的首席技术官兼首席AI架构师科拉伊·卡武克丘奥卢将成为该部门的高级副总裁，并负责其运营，包括开发谷歌旗舰前沿模型和产品，即Gemini。长期担任谷歌工程师的杰夫·迪恩在近三十年后也离开公司，以“尝试新事物，我们很高兴支持他这样做，”谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊在宣布此消息的博客文章中表示。哈萨比斯于2010年共同创立了DeepMind，四年后，据当时报道，谷歌以6.5亿美元收购了该研究实验室。他的联合创始人穆斯塔法·苏莱曼目前是微软AI部门的主管。谷歌正在与其他主要AI开发者竞争客户，包括微软、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，以及中国的DeepSeek和Moonshot。

paragraphs.en: The industry is also chasing a {{8}} {{7}} known as advanced general intelligence (AGI), which is a point when AI software matches the {{9}} of human thinking. "I've been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at {{11}}," Hassabis wrote in Wednesday's blog post. "With this {{10}}, I've decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at (Google DeepMind), so that I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help {{12}} what is to come," Hassabis continued. Observers have been waiting for Google to announce a more powerful version of its AI model, called Gemini 3.5 Pro, which was supposed to launch in June but appears to be {{13}}. Its shares closed 4% down Wednesday afternoon.
paragraphs.cn: 该行业还在追逐一个理论里程碑，即高级通用智能（AGI），这是AI软件达到人类思维能力水平的时刻。“我一生都在致力于AGI，现在，像你们中的许多人一样，我觉得它近在眼前，”哈萨比斯在周三的博客文章中写道。“在这种背景下，我决定现在是时候将我在（谷歌DeepMind）的日常运营职责移交出去，以便我有时间和空间专注于大局，并帮助影响未来，”哈萨比斯继续说道。观察者一直在等待谷歌宣布其AI模型的更强大版本，称为Gemini 3.5 Pro，该模型原定于6月推出，但似乎被推迟。其股价周三下午收盘下跌4%。

paragraphs.en: The leadership changes come amid a wider brain {{14}} at Google. In June, a top AI and engineering executive, Noam Shazeer, left for OpenAI, while senior researcher John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry with Hassabis, {{15}} to Anthropic.
paragraphs.cn: 领导层变动发生在谷歌更广泛的人才流失背景下。6月，一位顶级AI和工程高管诺姆·沙泽尔离开去了OpenAI，而高级研究员约翰·詹珀，与哈萨比斯共同获得2024年诺贝尔化学奖，跳槽到了Anthropic。

articles.fullText:
Google's head of AI, Demis Hassabis, will step down from his current role to become Alphabet's chief scientist amid a reshuffling at DeepMind that will also include a key engineer's departure.
Hassabis will take on two new titles, Alphabet announced on Wednesday: chair of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet.
The change "will allow me to focus on long-term strategy, and accelerating scientific breakthroughs, including leaning into my work at Isomorphic to help cure disease," Hassabis wrote in a social media post.
Isomorphic Labs is an AI-powered drug discovery lab that spun out from DeepMind in 2021. In 2024, Hassabis won a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
As part of the shake up, DeepMind's chief technology officer and chief AI architect Koray Kavukcuoglu will become the division's senior vice president and oversee its operations, including the development of Google's flagship frontier models and products which are known as Gemini.
Longtime Google engineer Jeff Dean is also leaving the company after nearly three decades to "try something new, and we're excited to support him in that," Google CEO Sundar Pichai said in a blog post announcing the news.
Hassabis co-founded DeepMind in 2010, and four years later, Google bought the research lab for $650 million, according to reports at the time. His co-founder, Mustafa Suleyman, is currently the chief of Microsoft's AI segment.
Google is competing for customers alongside other major AI developers including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, as well as DeepSeek and Moonshot in China.
The industry is also chasing a theoretical milestone known as advanced general intelligence (AGI), which is a point when AI software matches the capabilities of human thinking.
"I've been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand," Hassabis wrote in Wednesday's blog post.
"With this backdrop, I've decided that now is the right time for me to hand over my day-to-day operational responsibilities at (Google DeepMind), so that I have the time and space to focus on the big picture and help influence what is to come," Hassabis continued.
Observers have been waiting for Google to announce a more powerful version of its AI model, called Gemini 3.5 Pro, which was supposed to launch in June but appears to be delayed.
Its shares closed 4% down Wednesday afternoon.
The leadership changes come amid a wider brain drain at Google.
In June, a top AI and engineering executive, Noam Shazeer, left for OpenAI, while senior researcher John Jumper, who shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in chemistry with Hassabis, jumped to Anthropic.

谷歌AI负责人德米斯·哈萨比斯将卸任当前职务，成为Alphabet的首席科学家，与此同时DeepMind进行重组，包括一位关键工程师的离职。Alphabet于周三宣布，哈萨比斯将担任两个新职务：DeepMind主席和Alphabet首席科学家。哈萨比斯在社交媒体帖子中写道，这一变动“将使我能够专注于长期战略，并加速科学突破，包括深入我在Isomorphic的工作以帮助治愈疾病。”Isomorphic Labs是一个AI驱动的药物发现实验室，于2021年从DeepMind分拆出来。2024年，哈萨比斯获得了诺贝尔化学奖。

作为重组的一部分，DeepMind的首席技术官兼首席AI架构师科拉伊·卡武克丘奥卢将成为该部门的高级副总裁，并负责其运营，包括开发谷歌旗舰前沿模型和产品，即Gemini。长期担任谷歌工程师的杰夫·迪恩在近三十年后也离开公司，以“尝试新事物，我们很高兴支持他这样做，”谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊在宣布此消息的博客文章中表示。哈萨比斯于2010年共同创立了DeepMind，四年后，据当时报道，谷歌以6.5亿美元收购了该研究实验室。他的联合创始人穆斯塔法·苏莱曼目前是微软AI部门的主管。谷歌正在与其他主要AI开发者竞争客户，包括微软、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，以及中国的DeepSeek和Moonshot。

该行业还在追逐一个理论里程碑，即高级通用智能（AGI），这是AI软件达到人类思维能力水平的时刻。“我一生都在致力于AGI，现在，像你们中的许多人一样，我觉得它近在眼前，”哈萨比斯在周三的博客文章中写道。“在这种背景下，我决定现在是时候将我在（谷歌DeepMind）的日常运营职责移交出去，以便我有时间和空间专注于大局，并帮助影响未来，”哈萨比斯继续说道。观察者一直在等待谷歌宣布其AI模型的更强大版本，称为Gemini 3.5 Pro，该模型原定于6月推出，但似乎被推迟。其股价周三下午收盘下跌4%。

领导层变动发生在谷歌更广泛的人才流失背景下。6月，一位顶级AI和工程高管诺姆·沙泽尔离开去了OpenAI，而高级研究员约翰·詹珀，与哈萨比斯共同获得2024年诺贝尔化学奖，跳槽到了Anthropic。
